newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament to begin 4-day budget debate.
newsitem.headline: German parliament to begin 4-day budget debate.

text.p: The Bundestag lower house of parliament was to begin a four-day debate on Tuesday on a 1997 austerity budget intended to put Germany in the vanguard of European monetary union.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel has hammered out a federal spending package which will limit new borrowing to 53.3 billion marks.

Taken together with states and municipalities, Waigel is aiming for Germany's total public sector deficit to undershoot the Maastricht treaty's borrowing ceiling with room to spare, with new borrowing at 2.5 percent of gross domestic product.
Maastricht sets a deficit ceiling of three percent.
Waigel, 57, is bedridden with a cold and is unlikely to rejoin the debate on his ninth budget before the final vote on Friday, a spokesman said on Monday.

The budget package, which envisages a 2.5 percent cut in federal spending next year to 440 billion marks, will be the subject of heated debate but should clear the lower house intact thanks to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's 10-seat majority.
But the 1997 tax bill, which is subject to approval by the Bundesrat upper house of parliament, has an uncertain fate after being blocked by the Social Democrat (SPD) upper house majority.
